subject: Lumenix fallthrough behavior & SLO deltas — proposed tests and runbook
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@lumenix.com>, Jason Li <jason.li@lumenix.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lumenix fallthrough behavior & SLO deltas — proposed tests and runbook

Hi Emily + Jason —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Two quick recaps so we’re aligned before we hand anything to ops:

1) Your primary concerns (as I heard them):
   - How Redwood handles sudden regional outages and whether traffic falls back to the hostable region without request loss.
   - Rate-limit enforcement and burst behavior at peak (what triggers 429s vs queuing).
   - Differences vs the public hyperscaler APIs you tested (particularly error surface & observability).

2) Our high-level positions:
   - Fallthroughs: we support policy-based routing + automatic model-variant fallback (e.g., switch to compact quantized variant during resource pressure) — preserves throughput with predictable tail latency.
   - Rate limits: per-route token-based throttles with graceful queuing + token-cost visibility so you can tune headroom (we don’t drop bursts until configured error-budget thresholds).
   - Observability: per-request tracing + token-level cost + error budget alerts you can map to SLOs in your pager.

Proposed next steps (short list, actionable):
   A) Redwood -> deliver a concise test matrix for the three scenarios below by EOD Wed (I’ll attach a baseline).
   B) Lumenix to confirm success criteria (acceptable p50/p95/p99 deltas, acceptable 429 rate, max error budget burn).
   C) Joint runbook + 2-hour live test window next Tue or Wed (we’ll need: test accounts, target model version, target region, and expected traffic profile).

I’m attaching a first-pass test matrix (lumenix-test-matrix-v1.xlsx) and a short comparison doc summarizing the failure modes we see versus common hyperscaler workflows.

Tests we recommend:
 - Cross-region outage: simulate region A failure and observe failover latency and request success rate.
 - Sustained burst: ramp to sustained 2x expected QPS for 10 minutes to validate queueing vs dropping.
 - Error injection: force internal model runtime OOM on a subset of nodes to validate automatic model-variant fallback and error budget accounting.

I’ll loop Marissa from reliability to own the runbook once you confirm the window.

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: Lumenix fallthrough behavior & SLO deltas — proposed tests and runbook

Ben —

Appreciate the summary. Quick clarifications before we plan tests:

- Success criteria: our internal SLO is 99.95% availability on the inference path (excluding planned maintenance). For the evaluation, we want to understand how much availability degrades during failover and whether failovers introduce silent errors.
- Rate limiting: we observed in prior vendor tests that an upstream 5xx was converted to a 200 with an error payload — we want to ensure you won’t mask errors during fallback.
- Observability: for audits, we need request-level logs for 48 hours (including request body hashes), and exportable metrics we can ingest into our internal Grafana.

Regarding timing — next Tue morning (PST) works. Jason and I will own the environment and procurement will provision any temporary keys.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood provide a short runbook (play-by-play) for engineers so we can simulate the exact failure conditions?
2) Will you confirm whether failover will switch to a quantized model variant or route to a different region first (we want to know ordering and if there’s any in-flight request loss).

Thanks,
Emily

Emily Park
Sr. Platform Engineer, Lumenix Systems
emily.park@lumenix.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@lumenix.com>, Jason Li <jason.li@lumenix.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 08:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lumenix fallthrough behavior & SLO deltas — proposed tests and runbook

Thanks Emily — noted and thanks for the SLO target. Short answers up front:
 - We will not silently convert 5xx to 200; any fallback that returns a fallback response includes an explicit "fallback_reason" field and status mapping so it’s traceable.
 - Failover ordering: by default we attempt in-region model-variant fallback first (smaller/quantized variant on same pool), then cross-region routing if capacity still insufficient. That ordering minimizes cold-starts and preserves routing locality. We can flip the ordering if you prefer region-first.
 - Logs: we can stream request traces + request body hashes for 48 hours to a temporary bucket.

Attached: updated test matrix (lumenix-test-matrix-v1.xlsx) and a one-pager on our failover ordering (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-failover-summary.pdf).

Marissa — can you take the lead on the runbook and own the live window? Karthik will help instrument the metrics hooks we need.

Ben

Subject: Re: Lumenix fallthrough behavior & SLO deltas — proposed tests and runbook

Emily / Ben / Karthik —

I’ve drafted a runbook and the concrete steps we’ll execute in the live window. High-level: 3 phases (prep, controlled failure, observation + recovery). I attached the runbook (runbook-reliability-steps.md) and included the exact CLI/simulation commands. Key points / requirements:

Prep (T-48h):
 - Provide a service account + temporary API key with access scoped to test tenant.
 - Confirm target model version(s) and the acceptable quantized variants (we’ll default to q4b unless you specify).
 - Confirm metric export endpoint (Grafana remote write / Prometheus pushgateway).

Controlled failure (live window):
 1) Cross-region outage simulation: we’ll first withdraw region B's routing advertisement (simulate network partition) and measure p50/p95/p99 and success-rate over a 10 minute window. Success criteria: <=0.2% additional error-rate vs baseline OR explanation of long-tail latency causing request timeouts.
 2) Sustained burst: apply a synthetic 2x QPS over baseline for 10 minutes. We’ll observe queue depth, 429 incidence, and error-budget burn. Success criteria: 429s <=0.5% of requests OR documented tradeoff (latency vs drop) you accept.
 3) Model fail (OOM): cause a subset of model workers to OOM and observe model-variant fallback behavior and any retries. Success criteria: fallbacks must surface "fallback_reason" and no silent 200-with-error; end-to-end success rate >= 99% for the traffic that should be retried/fallback-eligible.

Observability & artifacts:
 - We will deliver a short CSV with request-level traces for the window (request id, status, latency, fallback_reason if any).
 - We’ll provide a short post-test summary that maps observed deltas to error-budget consumption and recommended config changes (batching, per-route throttle).

Schedule suggestion: Thu 09/09 09:00–11:00 PDT. If that works for Lumenix we’ll lock it and I’ll create a shared drive folder for artifacts.

Attachments referenced: lumenix-test-matrix-v1.xlsx, runbook-reliability-steps.md, redwood-vs-hyperscaler-failover-summary.pdf

Marissa
